body: The Nebraska Supreme Court ruled on May 8, 2026 (321 Neb. 335) that a county court lacked jurisdiction to evict a childcare business from a commercial property because the tenants' lease raised a dispute over title. The owner, an individual, had sued BB's Childcare, LLC and its principal in county court in December 2023, alleging unpaid rent under a lease that included options to purchase the property and provisions applying rent payments to the purchase price. He sought restitution of the premises, past-due rent, repair costs and fees.

According to the opinion, the parties signed the lease in September 2020 for a five-year term ending October 1, 2025, with possible second and third terms running to June 2035. Rent was $3,000 a month, and a nonpayment default required being 90 days late. The tenants could buy the property during the second and third terms with credit for rent paid, would have a purchase option if ownership changed during the first term, and would lose the option on a nonpayment default. The county court rejected the tenants' argument that these terms created a title dispute and entered judgment for the owner in February 2024. On appeal, the Douglas County District Court affirmed without reaching the merits, because the tenants had not included the county court's judgment in the appeal transcript, and it refused to accept a late supplemental transcript.

The Supreme Court held that the district court abused its discretion in refusing the supplemental transcript, because it was needed to decide whether the county court had jurisdiction. Reaffirming that a court cannot decide a question of title in a forcible entry and detainer action, it agreed that the purchase option, rent credits and limits on the owner's right to sell 'arguably conferred an equitable interest in the real estate,' which was enough to divest the county court of jurisdiction. It disapproved the tenants' broader reading that a title dispute exists in every such action under a written lease, and it expressed no opinion on the merits of the title questions, which belong in district court. The court vacated the district court's judgment and directed that the county court's judgment be vacated and the complaint dismissed. The State of Nebraska, through the Attorney General, had filed an amicus brief supporting the owner.

timeline.label: The owner and BB's Childcare, LLC sign a commercial lease with purchase options and rent credits
The owner files a forcible entry and detainer action in county court alleging unpaid rent
County court enters judgment restoring the premises to the owner
Nebraska Supreme Court vacates and directs dismissal for lack of subject matter jurisdiction
